title: grund.toml
description: The configuration of a grund project. `grund config validate` is the authority; this schema serves editors.

grund_config_version.description: The config format version. Omitted means 1.

project_name.description: The project's name; in a workspace, also its alias in `§alias/<ID>` citations.

project_description.description: One-line description shown next to the project in generated workspace member lists.

reference.description: How a citation is written, and the project-wide grounding and inline-note defaults.

marker.description: The character(s) that mark a citation.

trigger.description: The typed sequence the editor and `grund fmt` turn into the marker.

strict.description: `true` reads only marked citations; `false` reads bare IDs too.

shorthand.description: Whether number-only citations are written out in full (`canonical`) or kept as written (`accepted`).

require_grounding.description: Whether every scanned source file must cite a declared ID; the default for every `[[kinds]]` row.

grounding_level.description: The unit that must carry a citation: `1` the whole file, `N` every `H<N>` section too; the default for every `[[kinds]]` row.

conversation.description: The repository's opinion on how agents render citations in conversation: `link`, or absent for none.

max.description: The largest lead that does not warn, counted in `unit`s.

unit.description: What `max` counts in a lead: its lines, its words or its bytes.

lead_size_warning.description: Opt in to a warning when a declaration's lead outgrows `max` `unit`s (`lines`, `words` or `bytes`).

inline_style.description: Whether an inline citation may carry a note beside it.

inline_note_suggested_lines.description: Lines past which an inline note is a suggestion (a warning with `warn_on_suggested`).

inline_note_max_lines.description: The most lines an inline note may take; more is an error.

inline_note_max_columns.description: The most columns an inline note may take; more is an error.

inline_note_layout.description: Where the citation sits inside an inline note.

inline_note_layout_check.description: How a note that breaks `inline_note_layout` is reported.

warn_on_suggested.description: Report notes past `inline_note_suggested_lines` as warnings rather than suggestions.

reference.x-grund-note: `inline_style`, the note budgets and `inline_note_layout` are rendered into the managed block's `rules` section, so after changing one `grund check` reports the block stale until `grund init` runs ([§FS-inline-citation-style.5.5](../functional-spec/FS-inline-citation-style.md#55-rendered-not-live)).

id.description: The ID grammar: the shape of every declared ID and section path.
id.x-grund-note: Numeric IDs keep their written digits in reports. With `format = "{kind}-{number}"`, a heading `# ADR-0001: Use Postgres` is listed as `ADR-0001`, and a citation of it links to `#adr-0001-use-postgres`. `ADR-1` resolves to that same declaration; its spelling does not change the heading's anchor. This applies to the default grammar and per-kind overrides in both config versions ([§FS-config.3.2.8](../functional-spec/FS-config.md#328-numeric-spelling-survives-reading-and-reporting)). `grund id ADR "Use Redis"` still allocates with a minimum of three digits (`ADR-002` when the highest number is 1); pass `--width 4` to mint `ADR-0002`. Existing padding does not set allocation width ([§FS-id.1.2](../functional-spec/FS-id.md#12-number-width)).

format.description: The ID template: `{kind}` plus `{number}`, `{slug}` or both; everything else is literal.

section_separator.description: The separator between an ID and its section path.

named_sections.description: Enable named section components, such as `## goals:`, matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`: a name at any depth, under a name or a number.

section_heading_levels.description: How a heading whose depth does not match its section path is reported: an error, a warning, or not at all.

kinds.description: One row per kind: where its declarations live and how they are read. `kinds = []` declares no kinds; leaving the key out keeps the built-in ones.

kind.description: The kind's name: the ID prefix of a citable kind, its `[citations.<kind>]` key and its `--kind` selector.

prefix.description: Removed in grund 0.13.0 and refused: rename it to `kind`.

folder.description: A folder home: each declaration is the H1 of its own file under this directory.

file.description: A single-file home: every declaration is a heading in this document. It is read only if its extension is in `[scan] extensions`, or, on a `values = true` row, as its value source by the value pass when it ends in `.json`, `.yaml` or `.yml`; otherwise `grund check` warns at this line.

title.description: The kind's title in the Project map, `grund list --summary` and editor hovers.

citable.description: `false` makes this a place: it cites, but declares no IDs.

index.description: The folder's index file, which must list every declaration; `false` opts out.
index.x-grund-default: README.md (folder kinds; `false` for a kind named E2E)

scan.description: `false` lists the kind in the Project map without walking it.

require_grounding.description: This kind's grounding requirement; it wins over `[reference]` and over `--require-grounding`.

grounding_level.description: This kind's grounding unit, overriding `[reference] grounding_level`.

values.description: Make every declaration of this kind a first-class value.

value_chapter.description: The chapter whose named children are values, in every declaration of this kind.

rules.description: Make every declaration title of this kind an executable rule sentence.

format.description: This kind's ID template, overriding `[id] format`.

resolve.description: How a missing external snapshot is reported: `must` as a dangling citation, `should` as a warning.
resolve.x-grund-default: must when fetch is set, else absent

fetch.description: The executable `grund fetch` runs to save a missing external snapshot.

scan.description: What the scan walks and reads.

include.description: Directories and files to scan, from the config root; every kind's home is scanned as well. A file named here is read only if its extension is in `extensions`; when it is not, `grund check` warns at this line.

exclude.description: Directory names skipped at any depth; a stub whose target sits under one is broken, because a target the scan does not read declares nothing.

extensions.description: The file extensions the scan reads. The default is `md` plus every extension grund's built-in language table names, so a language grund learns is read without a config change.

comment_prefixes.description: The comment markers a citation or declaration in source code may follow.

docstring_python.description: Read Python docstrings as well as `#` comments.

respect_gitignore.description: Skip what `.gitignore` and other ignore files exclude, stub targets included: a stub whose target they exclude is broken, because a target the scan does not read declares nothing.

color.description: Reserved: accepted and kept, with no effect yet.

relative_paths.description: Report paths relative to the config root (`true`) or to where the command ran, as `--path-base`.

exclude.description: Files `grund fmt` never rewrites: gitignore-style globs from the config root.

cross_refs.description: Whether `grund fmt` wraps citations in Markdown links, and the anchor style it writes.

enabled.description: `false` stops `grund fmt` from wrapping citations in Markdown links.

anchor_format.description: The heading-anchor style of the links `grund fmt` writes.

workspace.description: The sub-projects a workspace root checks, each in its own namespace.

members.description: Member directories, or a directory ending in `/*` for all its children, each checked as its own project.

optional_members.description: Members that may be absent, such as an uninitialized submodule.

include_root.description: Whether the root is checked as a project too.

citations.description: Citation direction rules: one `[citations.<KIND>]` table per citing kind.

default.description: What any kind may cite when no rule names the target; absent means `may`.

v1CitationRule.description: What a citing kind (or place) must, should, may, should not and must not cite.

default.description: What this kind may cite when no list names the target, overriding `[citations] default`.

must.description: Kinds each declaration (or file, for a place) must cite; a miss is an error. A file of a place or the complement that cites nothing is not checked by this key; `require_grounding` makes it a finding.

should.description: Kinds it should cite; a miss is a suggestion. A file of a place or the complement that cites nothing is not checked by this key; `require_grounding` makes it a finding.

may.description: Kinds it may cite, even under a stricter default.

should-not.description: Kinds it should not cite; a citation is a suggestion.

must-not.description: Kinds it must not cite; a citation is an error.

v2.description: Version 2: keys grouped by concern — `[schema]` for what exists, `[rules]` for how it relates, `[presentation]` for what grund writes. Every constraint takes one strength: `must` is an error, `warn` a warning, `should` a suggestion shown by `grund check --suggestions`, and `may` is not checked.

grund_config_version.description: The config format version: 2 selects the version-2 reader.

project_name.description: The project's name; in a workspace, also its alias in `§alias/<ID>` citations.

schema.description: What exists: the citation marker, the ID grammar, the sources, the note and lead measures, and the kinds.

marker.description: The character(s) that mark a citation, as v1 `[reference] marker`.

shorthand.description: Whether number-only citations are written out in full (`canonical`) or kept as written (`accepted`).

id_format.description: The ID template, as v1 `[id] format`.

slug_pattern.description: Regex for `{slug}`; the default starts with a letter.

section_separator.description: The separator between an ID and its section path.

heading_depth.description: How strongly a heading whose depth does not match its section path is reported.

sources.description: The sources a version-2 project is read from.

languages.description: The languages a version-2 project reads: built-in names from the v2 epoch, or names defined under `[schema.sources.definitions]`. Omitted, the epoch's default set; `[]` reads nothing.

declarations.description: Which comment blocks of a source file may declare an ID: only those the language's doc profile calls documentation, or every comment as in version 1. Citations are read in every comment either way.

exclude.description: Gitignore-style patterns, resolved against the config root, for paths the scan never reads. A stub whose target a pattern matches is broken, and the pattern is named as the reason its target is not read. Unlike version 1 there are no built-in names.

respect_gitignore.description: Skip what `.gitignore` and other ignore files exclude, stub targets included: a stub whose target they exclude is broken, because a target the scan does not read declares nothing.

extensions.description: Maps a file suffix, written without its dot, to an admitted language; an entry overrides the epoch's own assignment of that suffix.

additionalProperties.description: The admitted language files with this suffix are read as.

definitions.description: Languages of your own, which `languages` may then admit and `[schema.sources.extensions]` may map a suffix to.

class.description: The reader: Markdown, the JSON value-file reader, or the source reader through the comment hosts. Required.

comment_prefixes.description: The literal prefixes a comment is read behind, longest first.

doc_comments.description: The frozen doc profile that says which comments are documentation; `none` lets every comment declare.

docstrings.description: Whether triple-quoted Python docstrings are read as comments.

lines.description: How many lines an inline note may take, by strength.

must.description: The most lines an inline note may take; more is an error.

warn.description: Lines past which an inline note is a warning.

should.description: Lines past which an inline note is a suggestion.

may.description: A line guideline that is not checked.

columns.description: How many columns an inline note may take, by strength.

must.description: The most columns an inline note may take; more is an error.

warn.description: Columns past which an inline note is a warning.

should.description: Columns past which an inline note is a suggestion.

may.description: A column guideline that is not checked.

text.description: Whether an inline note may carry text beside its citation.

must.description: `true` lets an inline note carry text beside its citation; `false` allows the citation alone.

layout.description: Where the citation sits inside a note; write one strength only.

must.description: The required layout; a deviation is an error.

warn.description: The required layout; a deviation is a warning.

should.description: The required layout; a deviation is a suggestion.

layout.x-grund-note: Every `[schema.notes]` table is rendered into the managed block's `rules` section, so after a change to one `grund check` reports the block stale until `grund init` runs ([§FS-inline-citation-style.5.5](../functional-spec/FS-inline-citation-style.md#55-rendered-not-live)).

words.description: How many words a declaration's lead may take, by strength.

must.description: Words past which a declaration's lead is an error.

warn.description: Words past which a declaration's lead is a warning.

should.description: Words past which a declaration's lead is a suggestion.

may.description: A word guideline that is not checked.

rules.description: How nodes relate: citation rules, grounding and snapshot resolution.

citations.description: Citation direction rules: one `[rules.citations.<KIND>]` table per citing kind.

default.description: What a citing kind may cite when its rule does not name the target: `may`, or a prohibition at some strength.

resolution.description: How strongly a fetched kind's missing snapshot is reported: `<KIND> = "must"` or `"warn"`.

additionalProperties.description: The strength of a missing snapshot for this fetched kind.

presentation.description: The bytes grund writes: the trigger, the conversation opinion, kind titles and `grund fmt`.

description.description: A one-line description shown beside the project in generated workspace member lists.

trigger.description: The typed sequence the editor and `grund fmt` turn into the marker.

conversation.description: The repository's opinion on how agents render citations in conversation: `link`, or absent for none.

rules.description: Where each row's agent guidance is written: `home`, the `AGENTS.md` of the deepest directory holding the row's places; `root`, the root entrypoint, as a version-1 config renders it.

kinds.description: Display titles, one `[presentation.kinds.<NAME>]` table per kind.

title.description: The kind's title in the Project map, `grund list --summary` and editor hovers.

fmt.description: What `grund fmt` writes and leaves alone.
fmt.x-grund-note:
For another string value of `anchors` or `links`, the refusal names the supplied
value and the only assignment this binary executes. For example, `links = "off"`
on line 5 produces the following diagnostic. Quotes, backslashes and control
characters in the value are escaped so the message stays on one line.
[§FS-config-v2.rollout.fmt-values](../functional-spec/FS-config-v2.md#rolloutfmt-values-a-recognized-formatting-key-names-the-value-it-cannot-execute)

```text
error: grund.toml:5: `[presentation.fmt] links` is part of the v2 format but not supported by this grund yet; unsupported value "off"; executes only links = "index"
```

anchors.description: The heading-anchor style `grund fmt` writes in citation links; `github` is the only one today.

links.description: Where `grund fmt` points citation links; `index` is the only target today.

exclude.description: Files `grund fmt` never rewrites: gitignore-style globs, as v1 `[fmt] exclude`.

workspace.description: The sub-projects a workspace root checks, each in its own namespace.

members.description: Member directories, or globs of them, each checked as its own project.

optional_members.description: Members that may be absent, such as an uninitialized submodule.

include_root.description: Whether the root is checked as a project too.

v2Kind.description: One row: its places, its form, and its fields. A row may list several places; a file listed in `files` belongs to its row, otherwise the deepest folder holding it decides, and a file in no place belongs to `code`. The row named `code` is the complement: it declares no IDs, and listing places on it narrows the scan to every place written.

files.description: Files from the config root, in written order. A listed file belongs to this row even inside another row's folder. On a citable row with no folders, every declaration is a heading in one of these documents. A place is normalized (`./a/` is `a`), must stay inside the config root, and belongs to one row.

folders.description: Folders from the config root, in written order. Each declaration is the H1 of its own file under one of them; a file in nested folders belongs to the deepest. A place is normalized, must stay inside the config root and outside every workspace member, belongs to one row, and a folder may not link out of the project root.

citable.description: `false` makes this a place: it cites, but declares no IDs. A non-citable row must list a place unless it is `code`, which is non-citable by name; `citable = true` on `code` is refused.

scan.description: `false` lists the kind in the Project map without walking any of its places; a scanned place nested under it is still walked. Refused on `code`: narrow its places or use `[schema.sources] exclude`.

index.description: The index file each folder keeps, which must list every declaration that folder owns; `false` opts out.
index.x-grund-default: README.md (no E2E special case in v2)

id_format.description: This kind's ID template, overriding `[schema] id_format`.

fetch.description: The executable `grund fetch` runs to save a missing external snapshot.

form.description: What a declaration is: ordinary `prose`, a first-class `value`, or an executable `rule`.

closed.description: How strongly a chapter that is neither a declared field nor a numbered section is reported.

fields.description: The kind's chapters as fields, by name.

v2Field.description: One field: a chapter of the kind, its presence, position and content.

title.description: The heading title the chapter must carry, exactly.

presence.description: How strongly a missing chapter is reported.

position.description: Pin the chapter first or last among the declaration's sections.

after.description: Name of another field of the same kind this one comes directly after.

content.description: `values` makes this chapter the kind's value chapter.

one_of.description: The values a scalar chapter's title may take.

v2FrontMatterField.description: The file's front matter as a field: the first declaration's block, YAML between --- lines or TOML between +++ lines, its top-level keys the field's sections. It has no heading, so it takes no title, position, after, content or one_of.

presence.description: How strongly a declaration without front matter is reported.

closed.description: How strongly a top-level key the field does not declare is reported.

keys.description: The block's keys, by name, in the order they are listed and reported.

v2FrontMatterKey.description: One top-level key of the front matter: its presence and the values it may take.

presence.description: How strongly a block without the key is reported.

one_of.description: The values the key may take, each a one-line scalar.

v2CitationRule.description: What a citing kind (or place) must, warn, should, may, should not, warn not and must not cite.
v2CitationRule.x-grund-note:
For a negative default that forbids a kind's own marked index entry, see
[index-entry repair advice](citation-directions.md) for the `may` edit and how
explicit prohibitions and independent rule sentences differ
([§FS-check.3.12.2](../functional-spec/FS-check.md#3122-repair-advice-preserves-a-required-index-entry)).

default.description: What this kind may cite when no list names the target: `may`, or a prohibition at some strength.

must.description: Kinds this one must cite; a miss is an error. A file of a place or the complement that cites nothing is not checked by this key; `[rules.citations.<ROW>.grounding]` makes it a finding.

warn.description: Kinds this one must cite; a miss is a warning. A file of a place or the complement that cites nothing is not checked by this key; `[rules.citations.<ROW>.grounding]` makes it a finding.

should.description: Kinds this one should cite; a miss is a suggestion. A file of a place or the complement that cites nothing is not checked by this key; `[rules.citations.<ROW>.grounding]` makes it a finding.

should-not.description: Kinds this one should not cite; a citation is a suggestion.

warn-not.description: Kinds this one must not cite; a citation is a warning.

must-not.description: Kinds this one must not cite; a citation is an error.

v2Grounding.description: The grounding ladder: the unit, by strength, that must carry a citation.

must.description: The unit (`file`, or every `h2`–`h6` section) that must carry a citation; a miss is an error.

warn.description: The unit that must carry a citation; a miss is a warning.

should.description: The unit that should carry a citation; a miss is a suggestion.

may.description: A grounding unit that is not checked.
